document.title: Usama Bin Ladin: Message Delivered to Taliban Representative (State 210511)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Mullah Omar Called Washington in 1998, New Documents Show
document.note: [Secret (NODIS)] Low-level Taliban official Syedur Rahman Haqqani says bin Laden 'is totally under control' and should not be held responsible for those he trained (over 20,000 trained for jihad). He says the Saudi attitude is unclear and that the Taliban welcome proof linking bin Laden to terrorism. Excised.

persons.name: Syedur Rahman Haqqani
persons.role: Taliban charge d'affaires of the Taliban-controlled Afghan Embassy in Islamabad

mentions.quote: SYEDUR RAHMAN HAQQANI, THE "CHARGE D'AFFAIRES" OF THE TALIBAN-CONTROLLED AFGHAN EMBASSY
IN THE PAST HE HAS DELIVERED OUR MESSAGES: TO KANDAHAR, SO THIS LATEST EXPRESSION OF U.S. CONCERN WILL BE PASSED ON TO OMAR SOON

persons.name: Usama Bin Ladin
persons.role: Terrorist leader harbored in Afghanistan by the Taliban; indicted by the US

mentions.quote: BIN LADIN WAS NOW UNDER FULL TALIBAN CONTROL AND IN NO POSITION TO COMMIT TERRORIST ACTS

PURPORTED TO QUOTE TALIBAN LEADER MULLAH OMAR AS STATING THAT THE U.S. WOULD "RECOGNIZE" THE TALIBAN IF THEY SURRENDERED BIN LADIN

events.description: US Ambassador Milam delivered talking points on Bin Ladin to Taliban charge d'affaires Syedur Rahman Haqqani, who insisted on trying Bin Ladin in Afghanistan and said he was under Taliban control.
Cable Islamabad 8410 reporting the meeting, repeated by State as 210511.
Ambassador Milam delivered US talking points on Bin Ladin to Taliban representative Haqqani; Haqqani insisted on trying Bin Ladin in Afghanistan and said he was under Taliban control.
Bin Ladin gave a CNN interview, later provided to the Taliban embassy.
Bin Ladin gave an interview to ABC.
Recent US indictment of Bin Ladin and Mohammad Aref.
Crown Prince Abdullah visited Pakistan and expressed concern about Bin Ladin's harboring in Afghanistan.
Cable Islamabad 08410 reporting the meeting was sent to State and repeated by Talbott.

key_claims: The Taliban charge d'affaires insisted Bin Ladin must be tried in Afghanistan because there were no extradition agreements.
Haqqani claimed Bin Ladin was under full Taliban control and could not commit terrorist acts.
Haqqani argued Bin Ladin cannot be held responsible for ~20,000 people trained for jihad.
The embassy judged Haqqani low in the Taliban hierarchy but a reliable conduit to Kandahar and Mullah Omar.
The US denied that surrendering Bin Ladin would automatically bring recognition of the Taliban.
Haqqani distanced the Taliban from anti-US statements by Pakistani nationals and the Urdu press.
